title: Southern Grid: a custom Microsoft Fabric demo
subtitle: Asset health, end to end

story.title: Which asset fails next, and what's it worth?
story.problem: Thousands of ageing network assets. The asset register, work orders and sensor readings sit in different systems, so nobody sees risk in one place.
pains: Asset data in on-prem SQL Server, loaded by SSIS
Sensor files arrive every 15 minutes, messy and late
Every new source means a new pipeline

measure.label: Outage cost at risk on the Gold scorecard (illustrative)

proves: One ranked risk list from three messy sources
Bad data is caught and quarantined, not lost
A new feed goes live with metadata rows only

architecture.title: How the demo is built in Fabric

stages.name: Landing
stages.desc: Raw files kept by load date, so any day can be replayed

stages.desc: Strings, appended per day, schema drift absorbed

stages.name: Silver
stages.desc: Typed, deduped, DQ checked, PII removed

stages.name: Gold
stages.desc: Risk scorecard with an illustrative dollar figure

spine.name: meta.* control tables drive every step
spine.desc: Sources, load type, DQ rules and PII treatment live in config, not code

notes.cover: Open with the business question, not the product: which asset fails next, and what does it cost?
notes.story: Southern Grid is fictional; every name and figure is made up. The dollar figure is illustrative.
notes.architecture: Walk left to right. Stress that the spine (control tables) is what makes it scale.
notes.moments: Run each moment live. Pause after Day 2 to show the quarantine table.
notes.takeaway: Point to the README Quick start. Offer to run a dry run with the team.
